verdict: Marvell's data-center revenue nearly doubled to $1.10B on AI demand, but a $715M restructuring charge — mostly asset impairments — pushed GAAP results to a $676M loss.

segments.name: Data center
segments.note: Chips for AI data centers — custom silicon, optics and Ethernet switches; 73% of all revenue.

segments.name: Enterprise networking
segments.note: Campus and small-business routers, switches and wireless access points; 10% of revenue.

segments.name: Carrier infrastructure
segments.note: Broadband access, optical transport and wireless radio gear for carriers; 6% of revenue.

segments.name: Consumer
segments.note: Broadband gateways, gaming consoles, home storage and PCs; 6% of revenue.

segments.name: Automotive/industrial
segments.note: Driver-assistance, in-vehicle networking and industrial Ethernet; 5% of revenue.

opex.name: Research and development
opex.note: Designing new data-infrastructure chips and platforms; up 2% YoY.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: Selling the chips and running the company; down 4% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring related charges
opex.note: Impairments and other restructuring charges — the main reason this quarter shows a GAAP loss.

footerNote: Marvell guided Q4 FY25 revenue to $1.80B ±5% — 26% growth YoY at the midpoint.
pngFooterNote: Marvell guided Q4 FY25 revenue to $1.80B ±5%.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $47.2M plus $0.5M of other loss, net, makes up the $47.7M outside operations.

takeaways.title: Data Center nearly doubled
takeaways.text: Data Center revenue hit $1.10B — 73% of the company — up 98% YoY as custom AI silicon programs entered volume production and interconnect demand stayed strong, and total revenue grew 19% sequentially to $1.52B.

takeaways.title: A GAAP loss, driven by impairments
takeaways.text: GAAP net loss was $676.3M versus a $164.3M loss a year ago, after $715.1M of restructuring charges — mostly asset impairments. Non-GAAP net income was $373.0M, or $0.43 per share.

takeaways.title: Cash kept flowing
takeaways.text: Operating cash flow was $536.3M, and Marvell returned $252M to shareholders — $200M of buybacks plus $51.9M of dividends — while guiding Q4 FY25 revenue to $1.80B ±5%.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $715.1M in the quarter — $356.8M inside cost of goods sold and $358.3M in operating expenses — mostly asset impairments, which is why GAAP gross margin fell to 23.0% versus 60.5% non-GAAP.

GAAP results include $158.4M of stock-based compensation and $264.9M of amortization of acquired intangible assets, both excluded from non-GAAP — that is why non-GAAP net income ($373.0M) is far above the GAAP net loss ($676.3M).
The GAAP tax line is a $74.2M benefit, not a charge, because the quarter was a loss.

sources.label: Form 10-Q for the quarter ended November 2, 2024 (SEC EDGAR)
